walkthrough:
**Recall the definition**

Think side by side with me. Homogeneous catalysis means catalyst and reactants are in the same phase. Heterogeneous means they are in different phases.

Rule to use:
$$\text{heterogeneous = different phase, homogeneous = same phase}$$

**Check each reaction phase**

Esterification uses liquid carboxylic acid and alcohol with concentrated liquid $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Ozone destruction uses gaseous $\text{O}_3$ with gaseous $\text{Cl}$ radicals. Atmospheric $\text{SO}_3$ formation uses gaseous $\text{SO}_2$ with gaseous $\text{NO}_2$. All are same phase.

$$\text{liquid + liquid, gas + gas = homogeneous}$$

**Spot the odd one out**

The Contact process is $2\text{SO}_2(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(\text{g})$ with solid $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$. Gas reactants with a solid catalyst means different phases, so this is the heterogeneous example.

options.A: Incorrect. In esterification the organic acid, alcohol and concentrated sulfuric acid are all liquids, so catalyst and reactants are in the same phase. This is homogeneous catalysis, not heterogeneous.
options.B: Correct. In the Contact process the reactants $\text{SO}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ are gases while the catalyst $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ is a solid. Different phases means heterogeneous catalysis, with reaction occurring by adsorption onto the solid surface.
options.C: Incorrect. Ozone destruction involves gaseous $\text{O}_3$ molecules and gaseous chlorine radicals, $\text{Cl}\cdot$. Both are in the gas phase, so this is homogeneous catalysis.
options.D: Incorrect. Atmospheric oxidation of $\text{SO}_2$ to $\text{SO}_3$ catalysed by $\text{NO}_2$ involves all gaseous species. Same phase means homogeneous catalysis, a common trap if you only remember it is an atmospheric reaction.
